description: Close-up photograph of a stainless-steel IWC Schaffhausen chronograph wristwatch with a silver-white dial, blued steel hands, black Arabic numerals, two sub-dials, and a black alligator-style leather strap with a deployant clasp, lying on a dark gray surface. The date window at the 3 o'clock position shows 19, and the hands read approximately 3:25. The dial layout is consistent with the IWC Portugieser Chronograph Classic. This is one of the wristwatch photos posted by Q, in which researchers read the time and date shown as a signal.
flags: Model identification 'Portugieser Chronograph Classic' is consistent-with, not certain
Any interpretation of the displayed time/date as a coded signal is the community's claim, not established fact

description: Screenshot of a verified tweet by Bloomberg editor Alex Wayne (@aawayne), dated July 22 2019, sharing a Bloomberg article by Anthony Capaccio (@ACapaccio) about a secret U.S. Army operation around Washington, D.C. The link card's photo shows two military helicopters in silhouette in flight — their profiles are consistent with AH-64 Apaches — behind a blurred American flag, though the article text refers to Black Hawk helicopters. The card headline reads 'Army Lets Slip That It's Conducting Secret Operation Around D.C.'
text: Alex Wayne. @aawayne. Follow. NEWS: The U.S. Army is engaged in a mysterious operation around Washington, D.C. By @ACapaccio. Army Lets Slip That It's Conducting Secret Operation Around D.C. description: Quote graphic from the AZ Quotes website on a black background with ornamental corner flourishes. A painted portrait of Napoleon Bonaparte in military uniform (cropped from Jacques-Louis David's portrait of Napoleon in his study) appears at left, beside the quotation 'Never interfere with an enemy in the process of destroying himself,' attributed to Napoleon Bonaparte. The attribution of this quote to Napoleon is popular but historically unverified.
text: Never interfere with an enemy in the process of destroying himself. ~ Napoleon Bonaparte. AZ QUOTES
flags: The quote's attribution to Napoleon is commonly repeated but not reliably sourced

description: Screenshot of Q post No. 138 (tripcode !!mG7VJxZNCI), dated 08/11/18, with an attached infographic titled 'Media Consolidation: The Illusion of Choice' — a widely circulated graphic claiming six media giants (GE, News Corp, Disney, Viacom, Time Warner, CBS) control 90% of what Americans read, watch, or listen to, comparing 50 companies in 1983 to 6 in 2011.
